newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: East Timor leader urges UN action against torture.
newsitem.headline: East Timor leader urges UN action against torture.

text.p: East Timor spiritual leader and Nobel laureate Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo urged the United Nations human rights body on Monday to act to stop torture and human rights abuses by Indonesia's army on the troubled island.

Bishop Belo, the most influential leader in the Roman Catholic-dominated East Timor, accused Indonesian security forces of routinely torturing East Timorese prisoners on the island, which Indonesia invaded in 1975 with tacit Western backing after Portugal withdrew from its ex-colony.

East Timorese prisoners are plunged into water tanks, burnt with cigarettes, showered with stones, tortured, slapped, kicked and punched, he said in a statement to the United Nations Human Rights Commission in Geneva from the territory's capital Dili.

"In the name of all Timorese prisoners, persecuted youth and oppressed families, I wish to make a plea for greater respect of human dignity in East Timor," said Belo, co-winner of the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize with independence leader Jose Ramos Horta.
Residents estimate more than 200,000 East Timorese have died since Indonesia's invasion, a subsequent famine and Jakarta's suppression of the island's self-determination movement.
Belo's fellow independence campaigner Horta, during a visit to Geneva last week, urged the U.N. body to adopt a strongly-worded resolution on rights abuses by Indonesia.

But it is unclear whether such a resolution will be adopted by the toothless Commission, where many nations refrain from criticising others for fear of being criticised themselves and countries like China often escape censure.
